title: Redis Patterns: Cache, Sessions, Rate Limits & Leaderboards
concept: Use Redis for what it is good at without trusting it with what it is not: data structures chosen by access pattern, cache-aside with TTLs, sessions, rate limits and sorted-set leaderboards, with PostgreSQL as the source of truth, invalidation that does not drift, and scores that survive duplicate and out-of-order events.
description: An advanced course for backend developers who already have Redis in production and want to stop being surprised by it. Every lesson starts from an incident on the CodeDev learning platform - a course price that stayed wrong for an hour after an edit, a leaderboard that lost every score when Redis restarted, a late event that overwrote a newer score, a login flood that took the API down, a hot key that melted the cache when it expired - and fixes it with a pattern you can test: choosing strings, hashes, sorted sets and streams, cache-aside with TTL, session keys, fixed and sliding window rate limits, invalidation, the source of truth, top N and rank, versioned score updates, rebuilding from the event log, stampedes and hot keys, and operating memory, eviction and persistence. 12 lessons with True/False quizzes on real commands, logs and timelines, and TypeScript challenges graded by hidden tests on an in-memory Redis model.

learningOutcomes.text: Choose a Redis data structure by access pattern: strings, hashes, sorted sets or streams
Cache with cache-aside and sensible TTLs, and keep sessions in keys that expire
Keep the database as the source of truth and invalidate the cache so it does not drift
Build leaderboards with sorted sets that survive duplicate and out-of-order events and can be rebuilt
Protect services with rate limits and operate Redis safely: memory, eviction, persistence and hot keys

testedVersions.Redis: 7.x / 8.x commands in lesson examples (in-memory model in challenges)

knownIssues: No Redis in the code runner: challenges use an in-memory model of the Redis commands they need (TTL on a fake clock, sorted sets)

Session keys with TTL: create, extend & delete

Rate limits with Redis: fixed & sliding windows
Spot the AI mistake: Redis as the source of truth
Leaderboards with sorted sets: top N & a learner's rank
Apply only newer events: versioned score updates
Rebuild the leaderboard from the event log
Cache drift & duplicate events: when late events overwrite new scores
